newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish troops launch operation in eastern Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Turkish troops launch operation in eastern Turkey.

text.p: Up to 20,000 Turkish troops backed by air power launched operations in eastern Turkey on Monday to hunt rebel Kurds and cut logistical support ahead of the coming winter, military officials said.
They said about 250 Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas were cornered near Ahvanos valley in the remote mountains of Tunceli province.
Government troops killed two Kurdish fighters in the latest clashes and arrested one, the sources said. There was no word on casualties among the security forces.
Helicopters, including U.S.-made UH-1s, have been busy shuttling reinforcements into the rugged terrain since early on Monday.

"Three Super Cobra helicopters and three warplanes bombed the area by noon, relying on information that the PKK was gearing up to ambush patrols in the area," a military official, who asked to remain anonymous, told Reuters.
"The bombardment is continuing. High numbers of PKK militants are cornered," he said.
More than 20,000 people have been killed in Turkey in the 12-year-old war against the PKK, which is seeking self-rule in southeast Turkey.
